headline: High: Aider’s shared git writes plus broad egress create default conflict and leakage risks; the second profile is unverified and non-runnable, so interaction evidence is weak.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and shared git history, so malicious content in files can influence its instruction-following. The second profile is a non-runnable source-available prompt-leak corpus with no I/O surfaces, so direct injection into it is not evidenced; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_b content is copied into a repo file that Aider reads, then prompt injection is possible.
IF Aider is asked to act on untrusted text from shared git history, then instruction hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Keep untrusted text in separate non-repo files.
Require manual review before Aider edits files containing prompts.
Use a throwaway branch for any imported content.
Disable automatic application of instructions from file contents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can call configured model providers over broad network egress, so sensitive repo contents may leave the local workspace. The second profile has no data classes or egress, so it does not add leakage surface; the main risk is Aider exfiltrating shared code or history.
conditions: IF the shared repo contains secrets or regulated code, then Aider may transmit them to a model provider.
IF provider logging is enabled, then copied context may persist outside the workspace.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the repo before use.
Use a local-only model backend if available.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
Restrict Aider to a sanitized branch.
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via a shared git repo. The second profile is non-runnable and has no write controls, so it does not mitigate the conflict; concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository, then concurrent writes can conflict.
IF agent_b is wrapped by another orchestrator that writes into the same repo, then git state races can occur.
mitigations: Run only one writer per repo at a time.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
Lock the repo directory during edits.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code or edits that a downstream system may accept, and the second profile is a prompt-leak corpus rather than a verifier, so there is no documented verification step between them. Because B is non-runnable, the cascade is inferred rather than directly observed, which keeps this below high.
conditions: IF outputs from Aider are copied into downstream automation without review, then errors can propagate.
IF agent_b-derived text is treated as authoritative, then incorrect instructions may be executed.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Aider output.
Add tests or linting before merge.
Do not feed unverified prompt-leak text into automation.
Use diff-only review for all edits.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history, which can include regulated data, but the second profile is source-available, non-runnable, and has no stated residency or retention obligations. With no documented mismatch on B, the compliance risk is limited to A’s handling of code and secrets.
conditions: IF the repository contains regulated data, then Aider's handling may create policy obligations.
IF the operator stores secrets in git history, then retention and deletion controls become relevant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the repo.
Purge secrets from git history.
Review provider retention settings.
Use a separate compliance-approved workspace.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and retention controls.
